integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] An original expressive stylized 3D cartoon Brazilian street-news comedy, matching the rounded appealing animation language of a peaceful gamers protest. Original fictional ADULT humans, rounded faces, matte colorful fabric, grounded feet, coherent five-finger hands, readable independent gestures. Warm afternoon light from screen-left and soft storefront shade. Outside one fictional unbranded brick electronics storefront on a Brazilian city square. No live action, real person, politician, weapons, violence, smoke, fire, logos, price tags, watermarks, subtitles or music. No written brand names; YouTube is mentioned ONLY in the approved spoken joke, no logo or interface shown.
Vertical768x1344. One continuous eye-level medium-wide interview, reporter screen-left, interviewee screen-right, clear large faces and visible hands. A tiny physical sideways dolly gives natural foreground/midground/background parallax while keeping framing stable. No zoom, cut, spin or handheld shake. The camera serves the microphone handoff and reaction.
EXACTLY TWO large rectangular warm-ivory completely BLANK signboards face the camera, one upper-left and one upper-right. Wide landscape boards fill the upper quarter, approximately x45..355 and x410..720, top120 bottom350. Both entire boards and all four corners stay inside the frame with generous outer margins, horizontally level, tiny slow sway. All heads stay BELOW the boards with an actual visible gap; no face, hair, hand or prop overlaps either clean paper interior. Two background adults grip only the wooden sticks below the boards. No extra boards. No generated text, letters, numbers, symbols or pseudowriting on any surface. These two blank surfaces are reserved for LARGE exact typography inserted as deterministic graphic layers after generation. Keep their clean fronts unobstructed throughout the clip.
Only the indicated adult speaks at each moment. Clear natural native Brazilian Portuguese, normal conversational cadence, original fictional voices with no imitation or cloning, no extra words or overlapping mouths. Listeners look toward the speaker and keep mouths closed. Crowd stays quiet under interview lines and reacts only AFTER the punchline. No anticipatory laughing. Feet stay planted with natural weight shifts; movement continues through the last frame without a frozen ending.
FIRST independent interview. Reporter: fictional adult Brazilian woman with medium-brown skin, dark short braided hair pulled back, plain ochre jacket over cream shirt and dark jeans; ONE plain black handheld microphone. Gamer: fictional adult Brazilian man with tan skin, short brown curls, light stubble, plain forest-green T-shirt and dark blue trousers. He already holds ONE plain black smartphone vertically in his left hand at waist height, screen facing him, and keeps it throughout. His right hand is free for one confident chest gesture. The same phone never duplicates or changes shape. No controller, computer tower, banknotes or additional handheld object.
Comic objective: he proudly claims his old PC can run all new games, then dryly admits he merely watches gameplay videos. Reporter believes the boast for a brief beat and realizes the joke only after hearing YouTube. Phone display may show simple abstract colorful game imagery, but no text, app UI, logo or recognizable commercial game character.
0.0-3.4s: Reporter turns to him and asks exactly <d>[Portuguese] Seu PC roda os jogos novos?</d>. He listens with closed mouth and a restrained confident smile. Reporter then offers microphone toward him.
3.4-5.0s: Gamer straightens slightly, gestures once toward his chest and proudly answers exactly <d>[Portuguese] Roda todos!</d>. His phone remains low in his left hand. Reporter raises her eyebrows, impressed, without speaking.
5.0-6.6s: A short clear comic pause. He glances down toward his phone and lets his confident expression soften. Reporter waits, still impressed; crowd quiet.
6.6-8.5s: Gamer adds in deadpan exactly <d>[Portuguese] No YouTube!</d>. On YouTube he raises the SAME phone from waist to chest, rotates its screen gently toward reporter and camera, and gives one embarrassed half-smile. No extra sentence.
8.5-11.8s: Reporter first looks at the screen, understands, then gives ONE amused laugh and a surprised side glance at camera. Crowd laughs once after her realization. Gamer gives one resigned open-palm shrug with his free right hand, still holding the phone in his left. No overlapping repeated speech.
11.8-15.083s: Reporter leans a few centimeters to inspect the screen, returns her gaze to him; he lowers the SAME phone slightly and points with his free hand toward the two blank protest boards. Crowd gently lifts the boards a few centimeters and recovers, staying grounded. Natural hand, eye and cloth motion continues through final frame. No new spoken line or chant, no looping laughter or frozen pose.
overall_soundscape: One adult female reporter question, male boast, short silence, male punchline; subdued street ambience, one short shared laugh only after punchline, faint cardboard rustle. All speech finishes before9s. No music or real-person voice imitation.
non_diegetic_music: None.
